We are advised by the members of the Commission that none of them have received campaign contributions within the last twelve months.
The applicant or any property owner entitled to notice of the hearing may, within fifteen days after the date of the Planning Commission decision, appeal the Planning Commission decision to the City Council (Ord. No. 091-529). A fee is required for filing an appeal with the City Clerkâ€™s office (R05-14).
The Council may, within fifteen days after the date of the decision or on or before the first date following the first Council meeting after the date of the Planning Commission decision, whichever occurs last: 1) Confirm the action of the Planning Commission and grant or deny the application; 2) Set the matter for public hearing and dispose of it in the same manner as on an appeal; or 3) Amend, modify, delete or add any condition of approval which the Council finds is not substantial under the circumstances relative to or affecting the property subject to the application for a development entitlement. Any determination of the Council pursuant to this paragraph shall be conclusive and final.

MINUTES OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES,
  CALIFORNIA

  November 17, 2015

CALL TO ORDER

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was
called to order by Chair Thomas at 6:30 p.m. on November 17, 2015, in the City Council
Chambers, 340 Palos Verdes Drive West, Palos Verdes Estates, California. The Pledge of
Allegiance followed.

ROLL CALL

Present:  Kao, Evans, Hunter, Welch, Chair Thomas

Absent:  None

Also Present: Planning Director Sheri Repp-Loadsman; City Planner Elizabeth Corpuz;
  Assistant City Attorney John Cotti; Julie Cremeans, Minutes Secretary

  *  *  *

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

None.

CONSENT CALENDAR

5.  WT-128-15; Wireless Telecommunication Facilities Application for new equipment
  within the City right-of-way in the center median at Via Boronada and Palos Verdes
  Drive West.

  Applicant:  Crown Castle NG West LLC
  300 Spectrum Center Dr., #1200
  Irvine, CA 92618

8.  M-1063-15; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for an accessory structure
  exceeding the allowable height at the single family residence located at 1024 Granvia
  Altamira. Lot 2 & a portion of Lot C, Block 1750, Tract 8652. This project is exempt
  from CEQA pursuant to California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section
  15303.

  Applicant/Owner: Ron Moravek

Planning Commission  1  November 17 & 18, 2015
 MOTION

  Commissioner Evans moved to approve WT-128-15 at Via Boronada and Palos Verdes
Drive West, exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning
Resolution PCR-2015-0867 with standard conditions and the following additional condition:
1) The replacement pole shall be revised to a maximum height of 14 ft.; and M-1063-15 for 1024
Granvia Altamira, exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning
Resolution PCR-2015-0875 with standard conditions. The motion was seconded by
Commissioner Welch and was carried by unanimous oral vote.

OLD BUSINESS

1.  NC-1540/G-1558/M-1051-15; Consideration of Neighborhood Compatibility, Grading,
  & Miscellaneous Applications for a new single family residence located at 908 Via
  Rincon. Lot 9, Block 1630, Tract 7142. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to
  California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

Applicant:  George Sweeney
  3 Malaga Cove Plaza #201
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Owner:  Richard & Cecilia Hu

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Kao asked about silhouetting of the pavilion, and City Planner Corpuz responded
that a portion of the silhouette had been damaged and that the pavilion is almost totally enclosed
by vegetation.

Commissioner Welch asked about approving a conditional use permit in anticipation of the new
ordinance taking effect before the building is completed, and City Planner Corpuz responded that
the ordinance hasn’t be codified yet and explained the process and the legal nonconforming
status.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

George Sweeney (architect at 3 Malaga Cove Plaza) came forward and presented the application.

Commissioner Kao asked whether the silhouetting extends further than current proposal, and
Mr. Sweeney responded that it includes the solarium.

Susan Booker (933 via Rincon), Ellen Cheng (929 Via Rincon); Daniel Booker (933 Via
Rincon); Jim Nazemi (932 Via Del Monte); and Paul Huh (912 Via Rincon) all came forward
and discussed view blockage, massing, home values and overgrown trees and requested that the
structure be moved with a slight change of design.

Mr. Sweeney re-approached and advised that the structure has been moved back and repositioned
as far as it could be. The applicant could give up the solarium and remove trees, but the
neighbors are asking for unreasonable drastic modifications, as their views are minimally and not
materially effected.

Planning Commission  2  November 17 & 18, 2015
 Cynthia Hu (homeowner at 908 Via Rincon) came forward and advised that she met with the
neighbors and removed the solarium and some trees, which improved views, but there is no
middle ground with the last two neighbors, who have a small view impact.

Commissioner Hunter asked whether there would be a flat terrace on the exercise room if the
solarium is removed, and Mr. Sweeney responded that there would.

Commissioner Hunter then asked about tree removal, and Mr. Sweeney discussed the specific
trees to be removed.

Chair Thomas asked about the pillars and entry gate or pilasters at the driveway, and Mr.
Sweeney explained that there are pilasters at the driveway at a lower level than pilasters entering
the courtyard.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Hunter commented that he has no issues with the adjacent structure, but the home
is quite large for the neighborhood. If the applicant is willing to remove the solarium and
commit to the removal of the trees he is comfortable with I but concerned about the fence and
gate in the front.

Commissioner Kao gave credit to the applicant for achieving view impact mitigation, and if the
applicant is willing to remove a lot of those trees, it’s a net gain in view. However, there are still
concerns about the overall size of the structure, which is still over 3,000 square feet larger than
the next largest home, and the scale and potential impacts to privacy.

Commissioner Evans agreed. When those trees are removed the views for everyone will be
significantly enhanced, but there is still concern with the mass and scale of the project, even after
the adjustments. The lot size is twice the average and the floor area is two and a half times the
average. That’s excessive and sending the wrong message. The front entrance needs to be
understood as well.

Commissioner Welch commented that this is a very large lot, relative to what can be built on this
lot it is well below the maximum square footage, and it is reasonable to have a multi-
generational house be larger. Although it is not approvable tonight, if the solarium is removed
and the drawings detail specific trees that will be removed it would be approvable. It would
Considering that it has already been advised that it will be appealed, it would be a disservice to
the community and City Council to not have the silhouette up and new detailed drawings in order
to understand the net impact to the view.

Chair Thomas stated that he is in a similar position. The applicant is definitely on the right track
but hasn’t done everything reasonable and practicable to mitigate the neighbors’ concerns. A
detailed drawing will help everyone involved, and there is concern about the proposed pillars and
gates without a preponderance of that condition on the street.

Commissioner Hunter asked that the applicant also provide a larger scale version of the elevation
to be able to determine the size of the chimneys.

CONTINUED TO THE DECEMBER 15, 2015 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING.

Planning Commission  3  November 17 & 18, 2015
 2.  M-1060-15; Consideration of a Miscellaneous Application for an accessory structure
  exceeding the allowable height at the single family residence located at 2609 Via
  Segunda. Lot 6, Block 1715, Tract 6885. This project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to
  California Administrative Code Title 14, Chapter 3, Section 15303.

Applicant:  Julie Waldron
  6043 Scotmist Dr.
  Rancho Palos Verdes, CA 90275

Owner:  Thomas & Kimberly Schloemer

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Julie Waldron (architect at 6043 Scotmist Drive, Rancho Palos Verdes) presented the
application.

Mark Towns (2608 Via Ramon) came forward and commented that the pool bath blocks out
light, eliminates pastoral views and impacts privacy. The height measurements should be made
from natural grade, not the altered elevated grade supported by retaining walls. The project
dramatically affects the character of his backyard. Mr. Towns commented that he is not opposed
to the applicant but is opposed to the height and location and would also like to ensure the
integrity of the drainage is intact.

Commissioner Evans asked how many times there have been drainage issues from the pool, and
Mr. Towns responded that there have been four or five times in 22 years, mostly when he
homeowner would leave the water line running and overfill the pool, but also related to heavy
rain.

Tom Schloemer (homeowner at 2609 Via Segunda) came forward and advised that drainage has
not been an issue since he has lived there. However, there is a drainage improvement plan.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Chair Thomas asked what the future new Code would require, and Planning Director Repp-
Loadsman responded that the application would be required to have the same setbacks as the
main residence if it is a habitable structure, which this is because the bathroom is intended to
have people inside of it.

Commissioner Evans commented that he understand both sides of the situation, but the overall
impact is not a supportable solution, and there was discussion at the last meeting about doing
something more innovative.

Commissioner Kao commented that he is prepared to approve the applicant and also understands
both sides. The applicant has made some adjustments to the design and height that reduces
impacts, and this part of their backyard is not the Towns’ focal point, which is evidenced by the
Towns’ redesign, and this is the only feasible location for the pool house.

Commissioner Welch agreed. There is some impact, but it has been mitigated appropriately. In
terms of the property owner’s rights to have the structure, the application is within the Code,

Planning Commission  4  November 17 & 18, 2015
 with the exception of the height, which seems reasonable given the grade. In terms of blocking
light, it is on the north section of the property and will block minimal light only at sunrise.

Commissioner Hunter commented that he is looking forward to the new future regulations
because he opposed to putting ancillary structures so close to property lines, but since those are
not yet in place, he can approve this application.

Chair Thomas commented that he appreciates the applicant’s efforts, but the placement of this
structure creates a looming effect on the Towns’ residence. It is very close to a set of French
doors that go out to their backyard and loom over their property. If it was within the building
setback and not an accessory structure setback, it could be approvable. If it came back closer to
the pool and further from the property line in line with the intent and spirit of the Code that is
going to come into effect it could be approved.

Commissioner Kao commented that he could approve it with the condition that it be moved into
the building setback.

Commissioner Hunter commented that he has been swayed to see the structure moved.

Planning Director Repp-Loadsman advised that silhouettes are very expensive and time
consuming and suggested that Staff work with the applicant.

MOTION

  Commissioner Kao moved to approve M-1060-15 for 2609 Via Segunda, exempt from
CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2015-0858 with
standard conditions and the following additional condition: 1) The structure shall be moved to
comply with the required side yard building setback. The motion was seconded by
Commissioner Hunter and was carried by unanimous oral consent.

3.  WT-125-15; Wireless Telecommunication Facilities Application for new equipment
  within the City right-of-way on the corner of Cataluna Place and Granvia Altamira.

  Applicant:  Crown Castle NG West LLC
  300 Spectrum Center Dr., #1200
  Irvine, CA 92618

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Chair Thomas asked for confirmation that this is either/or, and City Planner Corpuz responded
affirmatively.

Jonathan Kramer (2001 S Barrington Ave, Los Angeles) came forward and advised that there
will still need to be an above-ground cabinet under either scenario.

Commissioner Hunter asked about flexibility on the location of the vault, and Mr. Kramer
advised that this is approximately the general distance.

Chair Thomas asked about painting, and Mr. Kramer advised that there is no restriction.

Planning Commission  5  November 17 & 18, 2015
 Commissioner Hunter asked about putting the equipment in an underground vault, and Mr.
Kramer advised that the power meter must be above ground.

Commissioner Evans asked about flooding or filling with debris, and Mr. Kramer advised that it
is about the location and that there is nothing here that stands out as unusual drainage, but he has
seen lines run from vaults to storm drains.

Chair Thomas asked Mr. Kramer to recap the scope of what the Commission can evaluate, and
Mr. Kramer discussed the public’s concern about radiofrequency emissions and FCC guidelines
and advised that the Commission can rule on time, place and manner and whether the project is
being done in the least impactful way.

Planning Director Repp-Loadsman added that the vault could impact tree root structures and
might cause removal of the tree for safety concerns.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Steven Garcia (Crown Castle NG West LLC, 300 Spectrum Center Drive, Irvine) came forward
and presented the application.

Commissioner Hunter clarified the options, Assistant City Attorney Cotti cautioned against using
the option that would raise rates, and Planning Director Repp-Loadsman suggested that the
applicant cover the differential.

Mr. Garcia and the Commission discussed vegetation around vaults, drainage concerns and
possible danger to the public.

Albert Solbes (1509 Granvia Altamira); Deborah Fox (1616 Cataluna Place); Don Briggs (1616
Cataluna Place); and Carlos Juelle (1620 Via Montemar) all came forward in opposition to the
application, citing concerns of flooding, proximity to children, risk to trees, public safety and
aesthetics, and suggested alternative locations.

Mr. Garcia re-approached and advised that Crown Castle has identified the best available vertical
element at that location and has two options that are simple and don’t disrupt the park. There are
also options to prevent flooding, and there is a need that this proposed network is trying to
address. It does not detract from the ambiance and is not disruptive of the park environment.
The is the least intrusive means, as identified by the City’s Staff and third-party consultant.

Mr. Garcia, Mr. Kramer and the Commission discussed the coverage maps to ascertain the
degree to which the coverage will change and whether there is proof that there is a gap in
coverage.

Chair Thomas asked what findings would have to be made in order to deny the application, and
Mr. Kramer advised that the Commission would have to find that there is no significant
coverage; however, the applicant is a telephone company with rights to access the right-of-way,
so it would be subject to time, place and manner.

Commissioner Hunter asked about other sites considered, and Mr. Kramer advised that he did
not observe a less intrusive site in the area.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Planning Commission  6  November 17 & 18, 2015
 Commissioner Evans commented that this is at a 5-way intersection, one of the most grand
intersections in the city, and the aesthetics are more of an issue in this application than a lot of
the others. This location is not a solution that’s good for the city.

Commissioner Kao commented that he is torn because if this does not move forward but there is
a significant gap in coverage, there might be an issue. However, this is a gateway to the city and
a public park.

Commissioner Welch commented that the community clearly thinks this doesn’t meet the
aesthetics of that location.

Commissioner Hunter commented that he doesn’t like the public park location either, but the
expert advised that there is no viable alternative location.

Chair Thomas commented that the residents are pushing to get more of these approved, but
nobody likes to see utilities put in anywhere. The denial of this application would set an
exceptionally high bar. These antennas go through an extensive process by both Crown Castle
and a City expert, and compared to other locations these are very unobtrusive. The City should
be fulfilling an obligation to improve cell phone coverage on the hill by means that are
reasonable and practicable.

Commissioner Evans agreed but pointed out that there are particular circumstances with this
particular location deserving of special considerations.

Commissioner Hunter discussed the City’s ability to control expansion later down the road after
approval, as this site would be particularly onerous.

Mr. Kramer advised that as a City-owned pole it cannot be expanded without the City’s
permission, but that would not be the case if the applicant plants its own pole. Also, every other
potential site in the area that could be viable was in front of a house, so this was the best site
because it had the least impact and had existing verticality. Moving the brown box to the location
of the vent closest to the pole and getting rid of everything else would be the least intrusive at
this location. Exploring alternative locations would be a waste of time. The best option is the
cabinet close to the post, close to the street and furthest away from the park.

Commissioner Kao commented that he would reverse his original thoughts and reluctantly
approve as presented by Commissioner Hunter.

Commissioner Evans also agreed that he could support the application if it is a consensus
opinion.

Commissioner Welch commented that based upon aesthetics he will be the sole dissenter, as
there is too much public testimony against it.

Commissioner Hunter asked about incorporating vegetation, and Mr. Kramer advised that
because it is a power meter location, Southern California Edison has clearance requirements in
front of the meter. Planning Director Repp-Loadsman added that landscaping would have to be
created further away from the cabinet but could still have a buffer and suggested some options.

Planning Commission  7  November 17 & 18, 2015
 MOTION

  Commissioner Hunter moved to approve WT-125-15 at the corner of Cataluna Place and
Granvia Altamira, exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning
Resolution PCR-2015-0864 with standard conditions and the following additional conditions:
1) The steel pole shall be burnished prior to painting. The pole and antennas must be painted a
flat dark brown, and maintained in the same condition thereafter; 2) All cables interconnecting
the antennas and all transmission equipment should run within the replacement pole. No
interconnecting cables should run adjacent to the replacement pole except as minimally required
to connect to the antennas; 3) The replacement steel pole is not a wireless tower for any purpose,
but rather it is considered only a replacement City street sign pole; 4) The steel pole shall be
designated as a replacement for the existing pole to be removed, and after installation, the
replacement pole shall be dedicated to the City for a fee of $1.00 so that it is clear for federal law
purposes that replacement pole maintain its primary use and function as a City traffic sign
support; 5) The equipment cabinet should be painted a color selected by the City to blend in with
the existing surrounding environment and nearby meter cabinet in the public right-of-way;
6) Permittee shall install and at all times maintain in good condition an “RF Notice” and
“Network Operations Center Information” sign on the steel pole at approximately 14 feet AGL;
7) Permittee shall ensure that all RF signage complies with FCC OET Bulletin 65 or ANSI C95.2
for color, symbol, and content conventions; 8) Attached speed limit sign shall be installed in
accordance with the MUTCD (Manual Uniform Traffic Control Devices) California Edition;
9) Attached speed limit sign shall be with approved hardware per the City’s Maintenance
Foreman; 10) A multi-purpose cabinet shall be installed in lieu of an underground vault and air
vents; 11) The multi-purpose cabinet shall be relocated to be placed in the proximity of the
mocked up vent closest to the location of the proposed replacement pole at the discretion of staff;
12) Appropriate landscaping shall be installed to screen the multi-purpose cabinet; and 13) The
applicant shall work with City staff to provide appropriate landscape screening in the general
area. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Evans and was carried 4-1 with Commissioner
Welch dissenting.

4.  WT-126-15; Wireless Telecommunication Facilities Application for new equipment
  within the City right-of-way adjacent to 2800 Via Campesina.

  Applicant:  Crown Castle NG West LLC
  300 Spectrum Center Dr., #1200
  Irvine, CA 92618

City Planner Corpuz introduced the application, per written material.

Commissioner Hunter asked whether this is a City owned pole, and City Planner Corpuz
responded that it is provider owned.

Commissioner Hunter asked whether it is generally in the City’s best interest to have City owned
poles, and City Planner Corpuz responded affirmatively.

Commissioner Hunter asked about signage on the pole, and Planning Director Repp-Loadsman
responded that there are a number of different things that would make signage appropriate.

Planning Commission  8  November 17 & 18, 2015
 Commissioner Kao asked whether there is a certain standard the Commission should be looking
at, and Jonathan Kramer (2001 S Barrington Ave, Los Angeles) came forward and advised that
this is probably still a very good design for future collocations.

CHAIR THOMAS OPENED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Steven Garcia (Crown Castle NG West LLC, 300 Spectrum Center Drive, Irvine) came forward
and presented the application and advised that the applicant could install poles and antennas but
assign ownership to the City at no cost.

Deborah Fox (1616 Cataluna Place) came forward and asked whether there is sufficient evidence
of gap in coverage and suggested the use of free micro cell towers to provide coverage in the
home.

Carlos Juelle (1620 Via Montemar) came forward and commented that the Commission can deny
the application if it finds the aesthetics even mildly displeasing and suggested adding coverage in
a way that protects the aesthetics of the city with a view to where it goes next, as the applicant
can do almost anything they want on a pole that they own.

Mr. Garcia re-approached and stated that he will leave the legal issues to the experts. Indoor
booster service does not take into account that when we pay a full rate we should expect full
service all the time, not intermittently. This location is the least intrusive and would be City
owned, so any expansion is limited by the City’s approval.

Mr. Kramer advised that the courts have ruled that in-home repeaters cannot be considered, as
they do not add to outdoor coverage.

Commissioner Hunter asked whether the coverage maps show coverage for a particular carrier or
all carriers, and Mr. Kramer advised that it is just one carrier, but the City can only look at the
application before it and cannot consider another carrier’s coverage, which could come in and
apply for its own poles.

Commissioner Kao pointed out that this is all the more reason to limit the number of poles by
owning them and choosing to collocate or not.

CHAIR THOMAS CLOSED THE PUBLIC HEARING

Commissioner Welch commented that he is very pleased with the new location with the
condition that ownership of the pole is assigned to the City.

Commissioner Kao agreed and added that being able to own the pole is key going forward, given
the concerns articulated by Commissioner Hunter.

Commissioner Welch commented that this is a non-vault location and it makes all the sense in
the world, given the topography.

Commissioners Evans and Hunter and Chair Thomas agreed.

Planning Commission  9  November 17 & 18, 2015
 MOTION

  Commissioner Hunter moved to approve WT-126-15 adjacent to 2800 Via Campesina,
exempt from CEQA and subject to the conditions as provided in Planning Resolution PCR-2015-
0833 with standard conditions and the following additional conditions: 1) The steel pole shall be
burnished prior to painting. The pole and antennas must be painted a flat dark brown, and
maintained in the same condition thereafter; 2) The CISH equipment cabinet should be painted
dark green to blend in with the existing surrounding environment and nearby meter cabinets in
the public right-of-way; 3) Permittee shall install and at all times maintain in good condition an
